- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is trending upward, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast slope.  
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day mean by 1–3% in recent examples — apply a 1.5% downward bias to 30d forecasts.  
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, forecast should not exceed 2–3% above recent high — cap at 2% above 14d high.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7), model overfits short-term noise — smooth 30d forecast with 3-day moving average.  
- If true outcome is below forecast by >2% for 3+ consecutive days, model is overconfident — reduce next forecast by 1–2% unless sentiment confirms bullish.  
- Sentiment >0.7 with low price volatility → model tends to overpredict — apply 2–3% downward correction.  
- Sentiment <0.3 with rising price → model underreacts — increase forecast by 1–2% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
